question_text: Find the coordinates of the point(s) of intersection of:

mark_breakdown.desc: Graph both equations or equate X^2 - 4X - 5 = 3X - 11

subparts.solution:
We graph $Y_1 = X^2 - 4X - 5$ and $Y_2 = 3X - 11$ on the same set of axes.
The graphs intersect at $(1, -8)$ and $(6, 7)$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The points of intersection of two curves are the points where their coordinates satisfy both equations simultaneously.
step_by_step: Graph the parabola $Y_1 = X^2 - 4X - 5$ and the line $Y_2 = 3X - 11$.
Use the calculator intersection function (or solve algebraically: $X^2 - 7X + 6 = 0 \implies (X-1)(X-6) = 0$).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Providing only the $x$-values instead of full coordinate pairs $(x, y)$.

subparts.solution:
We graph $Y_1 = -2X^2 + 5X$ and $Y_2 = 5 - 2X$ on the same set of axes.
The graphs intersect at $(1, 3)$ and $(\frac{5}{2}, 0)$ (or $(2.5, 0)$).
